stories.title: AJK govt removes Rawalakot mayor over allegations of 'anti-state activities'
summary: MUZAFFARABAD: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) government on Thursday removed Rawalakot Mayor Abdul Naeem Khan from office and terminated his membership of the municipal corporation over his alleged “involvement in anti-state activities”.

The notification, listing at least 28 names, cited a decision of a cabinet meeting held on June 5, adding that the AJK president approved placing “activists” of the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) on the Fourth Schedule.

Registration of 14 private schools in Poonch cancelled Separately, the AJK Elementary and Secondary Education Department has approved the cancellation of registration of 14 private educational institutions across Poonch district, including Rawalakot, Hajira, Jandali and Thorar.

stories.title: JUI-F chief Maulana Fazl among nine party leaders barred from Sargodha district for 30 days
summary: LAHORE: Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman is among nine party leaders barred from entering, residing or remaining in Sargodha district for 30 days, according to a notification issued by the deputy commissioner.
Meanwhile, several senior JUI-F leaders were detained in Sargodha and served notices for allegedly violating Section 144, police said.
Fazl-govt rift On Tuesday, JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman claimed he had been put under an hours-long “state siege” to restrict his movement.

stories.title: Roads blocked, traffic congested in several parts of Karachi
summary: Karachi Traffic Police (KTP) said that Superhighway, near Al Asif Square, had been closed due to a protest. “Both inbound and outbound roads are closed for traffic due to a protest,” police said, without elaborating.
In another post, KTP said both roads linking Ghaghar Phatak near Sassi Toll Plaza at the National Highway have been closed to traffic due to a protest.
It noted that the traffic flow was slow due to the incoming and outgoing roads being shut to vehicles near Al Asif Square, adding that traffic police personnel were present and managing the flow.

stories.title: Rana Irfan whitewashes Asif to win IBSF Men's World Cup in Muscat
summary: Rana Irfan produced a flawless 5-0 whitewash of Mohammad Asif on Thursday to claim the IBSF Men’s World Cup title at the Active Oman Sports and Entertainment Hub in Muscat, avenging his defeat to the same opponent in the National Championship final in January.
A safety battle on the yellow ensued, and when Asif erred first, Irfan closed out the frame, 67-48, with a break of 20.
Asif briefly edged ahead after a safety exchange, but Irfan seized his next chance and raced away with a break of 68 to win it 91-12 and move one frame from the title.

stories.title: Achakzai's proposal of national govt only solution to political, constitutional crisis: TTAP
summary: Earlier this week, TTAP Chairman and National Assembly Opposition Leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai had called for the formation of a national government and comprehensive constitutional and political reforms to steer the country out of the mounting crises.

TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Ahmed Yousafzai. — Photo via X/File He stressed that all political forces, particularly PTI and its founder, must be part of consultations before any decision on the formation of a national government.
The TTAP spokesperson cautioned that the national government must not become an alternative to the people’s mandate or a permanent political arrangement.

stories.title: JI, govt to form committee to further deliberate, implement recommendations on public relief
summary: On Nov 11, the government and the JI had agreed on the “basic outlines” of a proposed agreement as the two sides held their 10th round of negotiations on petroleum levy relief.
Moreover, the government in September launched the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme to give targeted relief to two-wheelers and vehicles up to 800cc, the premier noted.

When PM Shehbaz and Rehman finally met about a month later, they agreed to form a joint committee to recommend proposals for expanding the fuel relief scheme and for a phased reduction in the petroleum levy for the next budget.

stories.title: FoodAg signs $168m in deals, MoUs
summary: The exhibition brought together 400 Pakistani exporters from more than 20 agro-food sub-sectors and over 900 international buyers from 80 countries, including major global brands.

According to consolidated exhibitor feedback, more than 5,800 B2B meetings were held between Pakistani exporters and international buyers, with exhibitors reporting total expected business of approximately $900 million.

Representatives of international regulatory and institutional bodies held direct discussions with Pakistani authorities on food safety, halal certification, plant and animal health, quarantine procedures, sanitary and phytosanitary compliance and mutual recognition arrangements.

stories.title: New tier introduced in PM youth loan scheme
summary: Under the revised framework, a new Tier 4 has been introduced for loans exceeding Rs7.5 million and going up to Rs25 million, marking an expansion in the financing available under the scheme.
According to a circular issued by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) on Thursday, the bank rate for the new tier has been set at six-month Karachi Inter-bank Offered Rate (Kibor) plus 2.4%.
The government has also revised the bank rate for the existing Tier 3, setting it at six-month Kibor plus 2.4%.

stories.title: PSX edges lower in range-bound session
summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) closed marginally lower on Thursday as the benchmark KSE-100 index shed around 60 points amid subdued and largely range-bound trading.
Some 39 shares advanced while 60 declined, where ENGROH, EFERT and PSO contributed the most to the index gains, whereas PSEL, UBL and FFC were the principal drags.

Topline Securities, in its market review, noted that the PSX experienced a subdued and largely range-bound session on Thursday, with the benchmark KSE-100 index ending marginally in negative territory amid cautious investor sentiment.

stories.title: Court issues notices to govt, other respondents
summary: The Islamabad High Court, while hearing a writ petition titled LPG Distributors Association of Pakistan and others v Federation of Pakistan and others, has issued notices to the federal government and other respondents on a constitutional challenge to the revised Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) Pricing Guidelines approved by the federal cabinet on November 4, 2026.

The petition challenges the cabinet's decision, the subsequent letter dated November 5, 2026, the decision of the committee constituted under the impugned guidelines, and the authorisation granted to Pakistan State Oil (PSO) and Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) to determine LPG prices.

The petitioners, represented by Muhammad Azhar Siddique, Advocate Supreme Court of Pakistan, and Syed Mehfooz ul Hassan Shah, Advocate, contended that the federal government had substantially altered the existing LPG Policy 2016, duly approved by the Council of Common Interests (CCI), without following the constitutional procedure prescribed under Articles 153 and 154 of the Constitution.

stories.title: Provincial funds to finance water, coal, gemstone projects
summary: The federal government has decided to take additional funds of over Rs1 trillion from provincial shares to finance national economic initiatives including coal and water projects.
The federal government has told the provinces that the estimated revenue collection will be Rs15.264 trillion in FY27.
The share of provinces in any aggregate collection exceeding Rs15.264 trillion shall not be subject to any grant to the federal government, and shall be received and retained by the provinces.

stories.title: Local holiday announced in Islamabad, Rawalpindi on Nov 27
summary: A local holiday has been declared in the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) and Rawalpindi for Nov 27 (Friday).
A notification issued by the Islamabad deputy commissioner stated that Nov 27 “has been declared a local holiday within the revenue limits of ICT”.
Separately, the Rawalpindi deputy commissioner shared a notification on X stating that a local holiday had been declared in the district for Nov 27.

stories.title: Bilawal terms PTI a ‘political reality’, calls for restoring its trust in the ‘system’
summary: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Thursday asserted that PTI was a “political reality” whose trust in the “system” needs to be restored for a political reset to take place.
On Nov 17, in a hard-hitting speech, Bilawal had asserted that the governance system had not collapsed, but was rather “made to collapse”.
Bilawal contended that despite strong rhetoric by governments on ending corruption, they failed to do so as the accountability system was “used solely against political opponents”.

stories.title: ECP issues delimitation schedule for 9 KP districts, freezes administrative boundaries
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Thursday issued the schedule for the delimitation of village and neighbourhood councils in nine districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

In a separate directive, the commission also ordered that the boundaries of all administrative and revenue units in these districts stand frozen forthwith, with no changes to be made until the culmination of the delimitation process.

Separate notifications have also been issued for the appointment of delimitation committees and delimitation authorities for the disposal of objections filed against the preliminary delimitation in these districts.

stories.title: SBCA chief removed as CM Murad orders sweeping action over building collapse in Karachi's Baloch Colony
summary: He said public safety must remain the “foremost responsibility” of every government department and warned that negligence in enforcing building regulations would lead to strict action, the statement added.
Rescue workers also needed to enter the collapsed building, using sensors and vibration to find bodies before initiating debris removal operations.
On Wednesday, the now-removed East DC told Dawn it had transpired during the initial probe that the SBCA had given the approval for constructing the ground-plus-one-storey building to its owner.

stories.title: Ireland men set for maiden tour of Pakistan in January, to play three ODIs
summary: The Ireland men’s team will tour Pakistan in January for the first time to play three One-day Internationals against the hosts, the cricket boards of both countries announced on Thursday.

The visitors, according to the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), are scheduled to arrive in the country on Jan 9, and will take on national developmental side Pakistan Shaheens for three warm-up one-day matches between Jan 13 and 17.

For the hosts, meanwhile, the tour would be an opportunity to test their depth – especially through the Shaheens matches – and continue the fine-tuning process of their combinations ahead of the World Cup.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz reaffirms commitment to stronger Pakistan-Bangladesh ties
summary: Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening its fraternal relations with Bangladesh, emphasising the importance of shared history, cultural affinity, parliamentary cooperation and stronger people-to-people connections.

The premier expressed these views while hosting a dinner at the Prime Minister’s House in honour of Bangladesh Parliament Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad Bir Bikram, and his accompanying parliamentary delegation.

Pakistan and Bangladesh are two important countries in South Asia, with considerable potential to expand cooperation in parliamentary affairs, education, culture, trade and people-to-people engagement.

stories.title: Security breach case: IHC seeks replies from parties on Imaan, Hadi's appeals against their conviction
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Thursday issued notices and sought replies from parties on appeals filed by lawyers Imaan Zainab Hazir-Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha against their convictions in a security breach case.
Imaan and Hadi filed appeals in the IHC against their convictions on Nov 7.
The Supreme Court directed the IHC to decide on the petition filed by the couple in the case.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz announces committee to review, implement Jamaat-e-Islami’s economic proposals
summary: Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday announced the formation of a committee to further review and implement proposals presented by Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) aimed at improving the economy and providing relief to the people.
The prime minister said several rounds of talks had been held between the government’s team and JI on the Ameer’s proposals.
On the occasion, Rehman thanked the prime minister for the relief package and said JI had held talks with the government with seriousness and consistency.

stories.title: Other realms
summary: IT was a moment of pride for Pakistan when PAF officer Muhammad Zeeshan Ali blasted off into space yesterday morning alongside his Chinese colleagues, astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi.
As the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft entered orbit soon after lift-off, Wing Commander Ali became Pakistan’s first orbital astronaut, carrying with him “the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis”.
However, while a significant beginning has been made, it will be years before Pakistan can take the same strides in space technology as China.

stories.title: Trump says he asked Putin to 'pull back' military aggression throughout Europe
summary: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday he told Russian leader Vladimir Putin last week he would like to see Russia pull ​back on military aggression against territories throughout Europe in the hope it could lead ‌to a quick settlement of the war in Ukraine.

Trump met with Putin last week in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of the APEC leaders' meeting, part of a diplomatic push by his administration to address the war in Ukraine and broader security issues.

Kushner argued that Putin had ⁠shown "restraint" ​by refraining from using nuclear weapons despite the risk ​of the Ukraine war escalating dramatically, and that he believed Putin wanted peace and improved relations with the United ​States.

stories.title: Govt to limit additional fuel cost charges to consumers at 83 paise per unit
summary: The Power Division, in a statement, said it has “proposed a Forward-looking Fuel Cost Adjustment (FFCA) mechanism wherein the increase … would be limited to approximately Rs0.83 per unit (inclusive of taxes) for the period October–December 2026” over the September FCA.

The statement came while the public hearing was in progress at the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) for an additional FCA of Rs2.88 per unit for electricity consumed in September and its billing in December.
The petition for higher FCA was filed by the Central Power Purchasing Agency (CPPA) of the Power Division for all distribution companies (Discos), including K-Electric.

stories.title: Police use tear gas to disperse fresh Bangladesh garment worker protests
summary: Bangladesh police said they fired tear gas shells and used sound grenades to disperse protesting garment workers who tried ​to block a major highway on Thursday to press ‌their demand for better wages.

The fresh protest broke out a day after a six-member panel approved a 36 per cent increase in the minimum wage for garment workers, ​the smallest in four decades, despite weeks of protests and calls ​for the sum to be doubled.

Weeks of protests by garment workers have shuttered ​factories, blocked highways, damaged property and disrupted production in a sector that employs ‌more ⁠than four million people in a country of around 175m.

stories.title: Chris Rock and Will Smith reportedly remain at odds four years after Oscars slap
summary: Chris Rock and Will Smith reportedly remain on bad terms nearly five years after their confrontation at the 2022 Academy Awards, with a source claiming their relationship has deteriorated further despite Smith's public apology.
However, the National Enquirer's source claims Rock was unconvinced by the apology and believes Smith's team encouraged him to release the video to manage the fallout.
He's convinced his team forced him to do it to try and cover his butt," the source claimed, adding that Rock believes Smith has not fully accepted responsibility for the incident.

stories.title: Govt cuts petrol by Re1, diesel by Rs2 for Nov 27
summary: The federal government on Thursday decreased the price of petrol by Re1 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2 per litre for November 27.
The latest revision comes a day after the government decreased the price of petrol by Rs4 per litre and that of HSD by Rs5 per litre for November 26.

Read: Govt slashes petrol by Rs4, diesel by Rs5 for Nov 26 On November 2, the government announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: PIA restores UK flight operations after Norse Atlantic disruption
summary: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) said on Thursday that it had restored normal flight operations to and from the United Kingdom, a day after two flights were cancelled by wet-lease partner Norse Atlantic as passengers prepared to board.
Norse Atlantic abruptly suspended operations on Wednesday, saying its financial situation was “critical” and it needed new financing to meet short-term liquidity needs and continue operating.

In October, the airline signed an ACMI (aircraft, crew, maintenance, and insurance) lease agreement with Norse Atlantic Airways to acquire two state-of-the-art Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners, one of which arrived in Islamabad on Nov 1.

stories.title: Türkiye, Saudi Arabia sign defence cooperation MoU
summary: Türkiye and Saudi Arabia have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen defence industry cooperation, Turkish defence industries chief Haluk Gorgun said Thursday.
In a post on X, Gorgun said the agreement was signed between Türkiye’s Presidency of Defence Industries (SSB) and Saudi Arabia’s General Authority for Defence Development (GADD).
He expressed hope that the agreement would benefit both countries and thanked Al-Sulaiman and his accompanying delegation for their visit.

stories.title: MNA among senior JUI-F leaders detained in Sargodha: police
summary: Several senior Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) leaders were detained in Sargodha late on Wednesday, police said, prompting the party to demand their “immediate release”.

Sargodha Regional Police Officer (RPO) Sohail Sukhera told Dawn that Maulana Abdul Ghafoor Haideri, a member of the National Assembly, Malik Awais and Maulana Amjad Khan were detained at a house in Sargodha and served notices for violating Section 144 imposed across the division.

Leaders detained under MPO in Khushab Meanwhile, several local JUI-F leaders were detained under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance in Punjab’s Khushab district late on Wednesday, police said.

stories.title: US man indicted over death threats against Muslim officials, including Ilhan Omar, Mamdani, El-Sayed
summary: A North Dakota man faces federal charges over alleged death threats against several Muslim US officials, including Representative Ilhan Omar, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed, according to US media.
Patrick Harlan Dyrud, 52, posted anti-Muslim threats on X targeting Omar, Mamdani, El-Sayed and other Muslim public officials, according to a criminal complaint filed in US District Court.
Investigators said several posts threatened to "eliminate" the officials, included anti-Muslim slurs and warned that they would be in danger if they remained in the US.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz launches ‘Mehfooz Dawa’ app to combat counterfeit and substandard medicines
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday launched the “Mehfooz Dawa” app to prevent the circulation of counterfeit and substandard medicines, calling it “a major milestone” and saying the initiative would help restore public confidence in the healthcare system.
The prime minister was speaking at the launch ceremony of the Ministry of National Health Services’ “Mehfooz Dawa” app, which was developed to track medicines.
Earlier this year, Drap had set October 1 as the cut-off date for launching the barcode system to curb the sale of counterfeit and expired medicines and eradicate black marketing.

stories.title: US clears SpaceX to launch up to 1 million orbital data-center satellites
summary: The Trump administration authorised Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Wednesday to launch up to one million satellites as part of its plan to build data centres in space, raising concerns from some experts.
Starmind’s satellites will communicate with those already in orbit as part of SpaceX’s Starlink satellite internet network, which will then relay the data to Earth.
However, there are numerous advantages to locating a data centre in space over building one on Earth.

stories.title: Major economies balk at new US tariffs over 'unfair' trade
summary: Major economies from China to the European Union hit out at proposed US tariffs after Washington concluded its months-long probe into alleged excess production, potentially opening a new phase in trade tensions with both allies and foes alike.

China is among those facing a 20 per cent tariff, but US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the levies were within the bounds of existing trade negotiations with Beijing. “China understands that we’re going to have some level of tariffs.

Trump’s tariffs have targeted Washington’s friends and foes alike, and are part of a push in his second term to remake global trade by forcing countries to buy US products or produce their goods in the country.

stories.title: ‘To the moon and beyond’: PM says Shenzhou-24 mission ‘living proof’ of Pak-China friendship
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday described the Shenzhou-24 mission as “living proof of the ironclad friendship” between Pakistan and China, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

On Wednesday, Wing Comm­ander Muhammad Zeeshan Ali became the first foreign astronaut to board China’s Tiangong space station, marking a historic milestone in Pakistan’s space ambitions and Beijing’s efforts to expand its space diplomacy.
He described the mission as “living proof of the ironclad friendship” between Pakistan and China, adding that cooperation between the two countries had now “truly reached the stars”.

stories.title: Sindh orders SBCA to halt illegal construction, demolish unoccupied structures
summary: The Sindh government on Thursday directed the Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA) to immediately stop construction of all illegal and unauthorised buildings and initiate demolition proceedings against gross violations, particularly structures that remain unoccupied.
A day earlier, a six-storey under-construction building collapsed, killing four people and injuring 14 others.
In early November, part of a two-storey building near New Nazimabad Flyover on Manghopir Road collapsed during construction work, killing one person and injuring two others.

stories.title: 'Unbelievable catch': Swat's motorbike passenger becomes cricket sensation
summary: Returning home from work on the back of a friend's motorbike, Mehran Khan acted on pure instinct when a cricket ball sailed towards him, and he nonchalantly took a one-handed catch that won him instant global fame.

Read: Pakistan and cricket: The perfect love story Khan and his friend were motoring past a match in the Swat Premier League in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Mingora when the ball arched towards them over the boundary on Tuesday.

What did Mehran Khan, the man behind the viral one-handed catch on a bike, have to say about it? 🎙️😄 pic.twitter.com/f2hqnzVSuk — Cricinfo (@cricinfo) November 26, 2026 The moment has gone viral around the world and drawn the praise of cricketing greats.

stories.title: Yemen's Houthis claim attack on Saudi Arabia's largest refinery
summary: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Wednesday they had attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery, Ras Tanura, which sits ‌alongside one of the world's largest crude export terminals, as satellite images showed thick black smoke over the installation.
The coalition said later on Wednesday that a projectile fired by Houthis fell at Saudi Arabia's Jazan port on the Red Sea, causing minor damage but no civilian injuries.

Saudi ⁠civil defence said 11 people were wounded on Tuesday in a strike on a tower in Riyadh's financial district, the tallest building in the capital that houses the headquarters of the Public Investment Fund, the kingdom's sovereign wealth fund.

stories.title: Makkah pact nations to discuss Yemen in Islamabad meeting: Khawaja Asif
summary: The Makkah pact nations will discuss the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed Houthi fighters in Yemen when officials from the mutual defence agreement meet in Islamabad on Thursday, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has told AFP.

"Any threat to Saudi Arabia is a threat to Pakistan and Turkiye according to the pact, which is absolutely clear," Asif said on Wednesday, praising Riyadh's handling of the conflict with the Houthis, who hold swathes of territory in Yemen, including its capital Sanaa.
The defence minister declined to comment on how the pact would react to a direct attack by Iran on Saudi Arabia, and identified Israel as a possible threat to other countries in the region.

stories.title: Rana Irfan stuns Asif to win Snooker World Cup
summary: The one-sided final saw Irfan take control from the outset, winning the opening frame 96-46 with a break of 56 before extending his advantage with a 67-48 victory in the second.
Senzah responded by taking the third 71-35, but Asif regained control, producing a break of 78 in a commanding 102-point frame before wrapping up the match with a 93-0 victory.
Iqbal responded emphatically with a maximum 123 break to force a deciding frame, but Irfan held his nerve to win the decider 69-15 and book his place in the final.

stories.title: IHC extends stay on Islamabad LG polls for two weeks
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Thursday extended its interim order suspending local government elections in the federal capital by another two weeks and sought para-wise comments from the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP).
Justice Malik remarked that the commission would have to satisfy the court that the delimitation process had been completed in accordance with the law.
The ECP’s counsel maintained that the commission had carried out the delimitation exercise in accordance with the applicable law and issued an order on October 14 declaring the process complete.
